observations: Photo 0 is very dark and shows the back and side of a large television standing on a terrazzo floor.
The rear housing is a deep black plastic bulge with vent slots, the shape of a CRT tube TV, not a flat screen.
A power cord runs across the back housing.
The front screen is not visible at all, so its glass, cracks and picture cannot be judged.
No brand logo, model label or rating plate is readable in photo 0.
No remote appears in the photo.
The seller states the transformer is blown, so the set is offered as faulty.

identity.kind: faulty CRT tube TV, large screen, for parts

claims.evidence: No LG logo or label is readable in photo 0; only the dark rear housing is shown.
No front view, size label or tape measure in photo 0; the rear looks large but the size cannot be read.
No clip of the set failing to power on; the seller's own fault statement is accepted as the worst case.

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen
claims.evidence: The screen is not shown in photo 0, and by the seller's own words the set cannot power on to show a picture.
Repair history cannot be shown in a photo.

risks.risk: Fault is worse than a blown transformer: dead tube, damaged board, or missing parts inside.
risks.proof: Photo of the inside with the back cover off showing the board, flyback transformer and tube neck intact.
risks.if_unproven: As not working, for parts or scrap only.

risks.risk: Screen glass is cracked or burnt, which a rear photo cannot show.
risks.proof: A well lit photo of the front of the TV showing the whole screen.
Photo of the rear label with the model number, or a tape measure across the screen diagonal.
risks.if_unproven: As the smaller common CRT size.

risks.proof: Photo of the front logo and the rear label.
Photo of the remote next to the TV.

proof_requests: Well lit photo of the front of the TV showing the whole screen and the logo.
Photo of the rear label with brand, model and size.
Photo with the back cover off showing the board and transformer.
Photo of the remote next to the TV.
response.reason: Photo 0 shows the rear of a CRT tube TV and the seller says it is faulty, so it can be priced at its worst case as a non-working tube TV for parts or scrap, whatever its brand. A front photo and the rear label would confirm the size and brand claims.
